agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider accessible ballot marking equipment demonstration
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to receive a presentation from the Chief Election Officer and Deputy Chief Election Officer on accessible ballot marking equipment. This is an invited presentation, meaning it is for information and discussion, not a final decision. The demonstration will show how the equipment works to help voters with disabilities cast their ballots independently. Council will consider this information as part of election planning.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Accessibility Feedback Form reporting for June–August 2026
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to receive a verbal update on submissions made through the city's Accessibility Feedback Form for June, July, and August 2026. This report is being presented to the Access Advisory Committee by a Social Planner. The update will summarize feedback received from the public about accessibility issues, which could inform future city decisions on improving access for people with disabilities. No new rules or fees are proposed at this time — this is an information-sharing item only.
agenda_briefs.action_required: No action needed now. Watch for any future council decisions that may arise from this accessibility feedback.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Federal wildfire evacuation plan for Canadians with disabilities
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a report on emergency response during wildfires for Canadians with disabilities. The report highlights gaps in evacuation procedures that put people with disabilities at risk, noting that roughly one in four Canadians has at least one disability and that over 670,000 people were evacuated between 1990 and 2020. A proposed federal framework would require emergency plans to include accessible communication (e.g., alerts in multiple formats, ASL interpretation), transportation, and shelter options. This is under review and not yet approved.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor federal announcements for public consultation on the proposed accessible evacuation framework.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider DeafBlind communication access for aging population
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a report on the growing need for communication access for DeafBlind residents, particularly as the population ages. The proposal would explore how the city can improve services and support for people who are both deaf and blind. Council will review the report and decide on next steps, which could include new programs or partnerships to help DeafBlind seniors stay connected and access city services.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on DeafBlind communication access — this could affect how your business serves DeafBlind customers.
